prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct ValueRemover and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The index-overload bug is the one worth meeting: list.remove(5) on a List<Integer> does not remove the value 5, it removes the element at position 5, because the int overload wins over remove(Object). It is invisible whenever the value and a valid index happen to agree, which is why the checker needs a case like without([0, 2, 3], 2) where removing "index 2" and removing "the value 2" give different answers. The rest follows the usual pattern for a method that promises a new collection: a duplicated value catches the remove-only-the-first bug, and holding a reference to the mutable input catches the destructive one.
hints: Use a list where the unwanted value appears twice, such as [5, 2, 5, 7]. Removing only the first occurrence is a real and common bug.
Include a case where the value and a plausible index differ, like without([0, 2, 3], 2) -> [0, 3]: list.remove(2) on a List<Integer> removes the element at index 2, not the value 2.
Build the input with new ArrayList<>(...) and check afterwards that it is untouched -- the contract promises a new list.
